author: Ramprasad
description: Decide ACT vs SKIP on a USDC/WETH swap by chaining live Uniswap pool intel (The Graph, sponsor API) with a paid varanasi alpha signal (x402) and a RiskGuard authorization read. The final decision depends on BOTH services: no healthy pool data, no trade; no affordable high-confidence signal, no trade; no RiskGuard authorization, no trade.

services.name: The Graph — Uniswap V3 (sponsor API)
services.access: Public Gateway URL with your Subgraph Studio key (placeholder below — never commit a real key)

services.name: varanasi x402 signal service (our API via Bazantic x402 gateway)
services.access: Bazantic x402/MPP Gateway importing bazantic/openapi-signal.yaml; payer needs Hedera testnet funds (~0.01 HBAR or $0.01 USDC per signal call)

services.name: RiskGuard authorize read (Sepolia, view-only)
services.access: Public Sepolia RPC; contract address filled in after deployment — read-only call, no keys
services.method: authorize(action, riskScore) — reverts if identity invalid/revoked/expired or score over threshold

steps.title: Fetch live Uniswap pool intel
steps.when: When the user (or agent) asks 'should I swap / enter USDC/WETH?' — always the first step, before spending anything on a paid signal.
steps.why: The paid signal is direction-only; without live TVL/volume context it cannot distinguish a deep liquid pool from a thin or spam pool. This step grounds the whole recipe in live sponsor data (top-by-TVL alone is unsafe — spam pools fake TVL, so pin CURATED_POOLS).
steps.gate: If tvlUsd is missing/zero or symbols look like spam, STOP with SKIP (reason: no-liquidity). Never proceed to the paid step on bad intel.

steps.title: Buy the x402 alpha signal
steps.when: When step 1 returned sane pool intel (real TVL, expected symbols) and the user authorized micro-spend.
steps.why: Pool intel says WHERE liquidity is; the varanasi signal says WHEN direction has edge (LONG/SHORT/NEUTRAL + calibrated confidence + feature breakdown). The recipe's value is the combination — neither service alone answers 'should I swap now?'.

inputs.payment: $0.01 USDC (HTS) or 0.01 HBAR via the Bazantic x402 gateway — first call returns 402, gateway signs/retries

outputs.txHint: position-sizing hint string (not a trade instruction)
outputs.receipt.hashscanTxUrl: settlement proof link for the demo video

steps.gate: If signal is NEUTRAL or confidence < 0.55, STOP with SKIP (reason: no-edge). Optionally call POST /v1/score ($0.001) for the cheaper risk-feature breakdown first.

steps.title: RiskGuard authorize read → ACT / SKIP
steps.when: When step 1 shows healthy liquidity AND step 2 shows a confident directional signal — the final gate before any execution.
steps.why: Signals and intel are advisory; RiskGuard is the human's on-chain guardrail (ENS identity valid + not revoked/expired, risk score under threshold, allowance remaining). The recipe must never output ACT without this read passing — this is what makes the flow human-authorized, not just bot-advised.

inputs.action: swap-intent descriptor (pool, side, max-size from txHint)
inputs.riskScore: 0..100 derived from step 1 + step 2 (volatility, thin-volume, trend-exhaustion, spread-stress)

outputs.authorized: boolean — false on revert (identity invalid / score too high)
outputs.reason: human-readable rationale citing pool TVL, signal+confidence, and guardrail result

steps.gate: ACT only if pool healthy AND signal directional with confidence >= 0.55 AND authorize() does not revert. Otherwise SKIP with the failing reason.

ACT_requires_all: step1 pool intel sane (pinned pool, real TVL, expected symbols)
step3 RiskGuard authorize() passes (identity valid, risk under threshold)
decisionPolicy.dependsOnBoth: Removing The Graph leaves no liquidity facts (signal alone could green-light a dead pool). Removing varanasi leaves no timing edge (pool data alone says nothing about direction). The final ACT is the AND of both, gated by RiskGuard.
